clue.text: Persevere with inexpert driver when on tee

parts.note: L is the learner plate shown by an inexperienced driver
as can mean when, as in 'as the sun rose'
the letter T is spelt tee

explanation.surface: Advice to keep at it when a novice driver finds themselves on a golf tee.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'driver' and 'tee' suggest golf, but the driver is a learner at the wheel and tee is just the letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: To persevere is to endure or keep going, which is one sense of last.

clue.text: Inappropriate amount of sleep when dog-tired?

definitions.text: Inappropriate amount of sleep when dog-tired?

parts.words: Inappropriate amount of sleep when dog-tired?
parts.note: a short doze named after a feline seems the wrong kind of rest for someone tired as a dog

explanation.surface: A complaint that a brief nap won't fix real exhaustion.
explanation.definitionFit: A short light sleep, especially in the day, is called by this feline name.

clue.text: Delightful spot in which ramblers grew up

definitions.text: Delightful spot in which ramblers grew up

parts.words: Delightful spot in which ramblers grew up
parts.note: ramblers are climbing roses, which would grow in a flower bed, but the surface suggests hikers' childhood home

explanation.surface: A nostalgic memory of the lovely place where some hikers spent their youth.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for a situation of ease and comfort is literally a bed planted with rose bushes.

clue.text: African animals finding fruit around river

indicators.note: the word for fruit is wrapped around the river

parts.note: hips are the fruit of the rose
the Po is the great river of northern Italy

explanation.surface: Large beasts in Africa discovered eating fruit by a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Hippopotamuses, shortened in everyday speech, are large animals native to Africa.

clue.text: A good one who's late is 13 across, wrote Wilde

definitions.text: A good one who's late is 13 across, wrote Wilde

parts.words: A good one who's late is 13 across, wrote Wilde
parts.note: Oscar Wilde wrote that good citizens of the USA go to Paris when they die; 'late' means dead

explanation.surface: Quoting Oscar Wilde on where a virtuous person ends up after death.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 across gives IN PARIS; Wilde's line is 'Good Americans, when they die, go to Paris.' Together with 13 across this completes the theme film, An American in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of the United States; Wilde's quip is about where good ones go after death.

clue.text: Overly cute stuff needs to be cut

indicators.note: the cloth word must be trimmed, losing its final letter

parts.note: stuff is an old word for woven cloth, and tweed is a woollen cloth

explanation.surface: A fussy remark that some excessively cute material ought to be trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Twee describes something sentimentally sweet or quaint to excess.

clue.text: Upholder of French customs faulted André? Oui

indicators.note: faulted suggests the letters have gone wrong and need rearranging

explanation.surface: A Frenchman named André admits, with a 'yes', to being at fault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faulted' makes DOUANIER from the letters of ANDRE plus OUI.
explanation.definitionFit: A douanier is a French customs officer, one who enforces customs regulations.

clue.text: Votes for Republican president, not hard-headed

indicators.note: the first letter of 'hard', its head, is dropped from the president's name

parts.note: Rutherford B. Hayes was a Republican president of the USA

explanation.surface: A comment on ballots cast for a soft-hearted Republican leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Ayes are votes in favour of a motion, as in Parliament.

clue.text: Madame is upset about constant adherence to formal rules

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the constant
upset signals the letters of Madame and is are knocked into a new order

parts.note: c is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman is annoyed at being made to stick to stiff rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns MADAMEIS into ACADEMIS, and 'about' puts it around C.
explanation.definitionFit: Academism is rigid observance of traditional academic conventions, especially in art.

clue.text: Everyone in club longing to see movie great

parts.note: a wood is a type of golf club

indicators.note: the word for everyone sits inside the club and longing

parts.note: a yen is a longing or craving
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A golf-club member's wish to meet a famous film star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Everyone in club' reads as a golf-club membership, but club is a wooden golf club and the longing piece is split around the everyone piece; 'to see' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Woody Allen is a celebrated American film director and actor, one of cinema's big names.

clue.text: Dance music as end of broadcast on radio

definitions.meaning: a Latin American ballroom dance and its music
the last letter of broadcast is T, which radio operators call by this code word

explanation.surface: Dance music being played as a radio programme closes.
explanation.definitionFit: This is both an Argentine ballroom dance and the phonetic-alphabet word for T.

clue.text: Bones from skull and others — 13 across

annotationWithheld.why: Bones from skull and others — 13 across (9): ET AL inside PARIS, but '13 across' (IN PARIS) is both the container indicator 'in' and the leaf PARIS, one phrase doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Bones from skull and others — 13 across

clue.text: Capital location to complete movies starting elsewhere

definitions.meaning: being located in the French capital
the film titles An American ... and April ... begun in other entries are finished by these words

explanation.surface: A capital city is the place to finish films begun elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase locates something in France's capital and ends the theme film's title.

clue.text: As communicated by pilot, I land in Asia

definitions.meaning: pilots spell the letter I with this code word
a large country in South Asia

explanation.surface: A pilot's radio message announcing a landing somewhere in Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both the phonetic-alphabet word for I and a South Asian country.

clue.text: French horn thus associated with a French region

parts.note: cor is the French word for horn
sic is Latin for thus

explanation.surface: A French horn being linked with a particular region of France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French horn' is not the instrument here but a horn in French.
explanation.definitionFit: Corsica is a Mediterranean island that is a region of France.

clue.text: Rues the outcome of this activity in France

definitions.text: Rues the outcome of this activity in France

parts.words: Rues the outcome of this activity in France
parts.note: rue is French for street, so streets result from building highways, though rues looks like a verb of regret

explanation.surface: Someone regrets what came of an activity in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Building highways produces streets, called rues in France.

clue.text: See 10
French author negating conclusions of stupid fool

indicators.note: the final letters of each of the two words for stupid fool are cancelled

parts.note: a dumb ass is a slang term for a stupid fool

explanation.surface: Dismissing a writer from France as a stupid fool.
explanation.walkthrough: The ends of DUMB and ASS go, leaving DUM + AS.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexandre Dumas was a French novelist, author of The Three Musketeers.

clue.text: Saintly Frenchman in company of stars

parts.note: Michel is French for Michael, as in Saint Michel

explanation.surface: A holy man from France keeping company with celebrities.
explanation.definitionFit: Michelin is the tyre company whose guide awards stars to restaurants.

clue.text: Repeatedly appearing in command performance, old boy

indicators.note: the letters sit inside 'command', and again inside 'performance', hence repeatedly

explanation.surface: A veteran keeps showing up in a royal command performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Old boy and man are both familiar terms of address for a male.

clue.text: Raised stupid, weird thing when PM finishes

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means the word for stupid is read upwards

parts.note: dim means stupid

indicators.note: weird signals the letters of thing come out strangely arranged

explanation.surface: Someone raised a silly, odd item once the Prime Minister finished speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' makes MID from DIM; 'weird' makes NIGHT from THING. PM is post meridiem, not Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelve at night is when the post-meridiem hours end.

clue.text: Best time to be 13 across, going by air? Not for Browning

definitions.text: Best time to be 13 across, going by air? Not for Browning

parts.words: Best time to be 13 across, going by air? Not for Browning
parts.note: a song (air) praises this month in Paris, but Browning wanted to be in England when it came

explanation.surface: Debating the best month to fly to Paris, while Browning would disagree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'April in Paris' is a popular song; Robert Browning wrote 'Oh, to be in England now that April's there.'
explanation.definitionFit: The fourth month is the one celebrated in both the song and Browning's poem.

clue.text: Damned with no end of rancour, as his government was by Zola

definitions.text: as his government was by Zola

indicators.note: the final letter of rancour is taken away from the word for damned

parts.note: accursed means damned

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of rancour

explanation.surface: Zola damned his government with bitter fury.
explanation.walkthrough: Zola's open letter 'J'accuse' accused the French government over the Dreyfus affair.
explanation.definitionFit: In 'J'accuse', Zola charged the government with wrongdoing, so it was blamed by him.

clue.text: Flower of poetry parking in French vehicle

indicators.note: parking goes inside the vehicle word

parts.note: camion is French for a lorry
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A poetic bloom parked inside a French truck.
explanation.definitionFit: The campion is a wild flower, and Thomas Campion was an English poet.

clue.text: Art form that's the same in France, but with an accent

definitions.text: Art form that's the same in France, but with an accent

parts.words: Art form that's the same in France, but with an accent
parts.note: the French word for film as art is spelt the same but with an acute over the e

explanation.surface: An art form called the same thing in France, only spoken differently.
explanation.definitionFit: Film as an art form, which France writes with an accented e.

clue.text: Part of extended family, as opposed to people like 26?

definitions.meaning: 26 is Kelly, as in Ned Kelly the outlaw; the opposite of outlaws

explanation.surface: Distinguishing relatives by marriage from people like someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: Ned Kelly was a famous Australian bushranger, an outlaw.
explanation.definitionFit: Relatives by marriage form part of the wider family, and the word plays against outlaws.

clue.text: Ignore rag that's wrong in relation to new style of dating

definitions.text: in relation to new style of dating

indicators.note: that's wrong signals the letters of ignore and rag are in the wrong order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Telling someone to disregard a newspaper because it gets the date wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's wrong' makes GREGORIAN from IGNORE + RAG. 'Rag' looks like a scrap of cloth or a newspaper, but it is only anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gregorian calendar of 1582 was the new style of dating that replaced the Julian.

clue.text: Player of 5 13 across generally has two characters changed

indicators.note: two letters in the middle of the word generally are swapped for two others

explanation.surface: A remark that an actor in a film typically has a couple of roles changed.
explanation.walkthrough: RA in GENERALLY becomes KE. Gene Kelly starred in An American in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: Gene Kelly played the lead in the film An American in Paris.

clue.text: Sign French author's antihero put up

indicators.note: in a down entry, put up means the name is read upwards

parts.note: Captain Nemo is the antihero of Jules Verne's novels

explanation.surface: A sign hoisted by a French novelist's dark hero.
explanation.walkthrough: The French author here is Jules Verne.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a portent, a sign of things to come.

clue.text: See 24 down
Ma delivered 13 across a popular toy

definitions.meaning: the cellist ... Ma was born in Paris, delivered meaning born
a spool on a string that is spun up and down

explanation.surface: A mother gave birth in France to a well-loved plaything.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both the cellist Ma's first name and a toy spun on a string.

clue.text: Northern tributary of Seine — that's what we hear

parts.note: the Oise is a river that flows into the Seine

explanation.surface: A geography note on a northern river feeding the Seine.
explanation.definitionFit: Noise is sound, whatever reaches our ears.

clue.text: Sometime 5 13 across as strange enigma — why?

indicators.note: strange signals the letters of enigma and why are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: Asking why a riddle is so odd.
explanation.walkthrough: Ernest Hemingway lived in Paris in the 1920s, an American in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: Hemingway was an American writer who spent years living in Paris.
